transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Dana (Aurora Head of Platform), Michael (Aurora Security), Priya (CTO)
Link to shared deck: https://redwood.app/deck/aurora-private-vpc (shared during call)

Summary (auto): initial discovery for Private/VPC deployment. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; leaning Private for PHI handling and on-prem connectivity. Primary concerns: VPC peering vs PrivateLink/private endpoints, CIDR overlap, region availability, routing through Transit Gateway vs direct peering, egress IPs and audit logs, KMS integration.

00:00 Sofia: Hey all, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. quick intro, I am Sofia, AE on the account for Redwood inference, and Marcus is our SE who will go deep on networking.
00:12 Dana: Hey thanks, I'm Dana, head of platform at Aurora Medical. We own infra and network.
00:17 Priya: Priya here, CTO. I'll mostly listen in for compliance and timelines.
00:22 Michael: Michael, security eng. We'll want specifics on encryption and network flows.
00:28 Sofia: Great, goal today is to understand your constraints for a Private deployment. we'll cover connectivity options (VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints), region constraints, and any compliance ask - SOC2, KMS, audit logs. then outline next steps.
00:42 Marcus: quick heads up, i'll cover traffic flows and the pros/cons per option.
00:47 Dana: to give context, we're processing PHI, so data residency and no egress to public internet for inference is ideal. current infra: multi-account AWS, primary region us-east-1, secondary eu-west-1 for DR. we also have on-prem in our dc in boston with an existing site-to-site vpn.
01:08 Sofia: Understood. are you already running any ML workloads in those regions?
01:12 Dana: yes, model training in GCP eu-west-1 and a few batch jobs in us-east-1; inference today is a mix — a vendor-hosted API and some on-prem CPU jobs for sensitive flows. cost is also a concern.
01:26 Marcus: quick question on CIDR - do your us-east and on-prem ranges overlap? sometimes customers have 10.0/8 contortions.
01:34 Michael: yeah, we do have 10.0.0.0/16 in us-east and on-prem is 10.1.0.0/16. no overlap, but we do have another acct with 10.0.0.0/16 for a dev VPC that might cause confusion.
01:50 Sofia: good, no overlap is helpful. For Private deployment we offer a few connectivity patterns: 1) VPC peering from your VPC to our customer-managed VPC, 2) AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) into our control/ingress plane, or 3) Transit Gateway attachment for multi-VPC connectivity. Marcus, want to add detail?
02:06 Marcus: yeah. So peering is straightforward if it's one or two VPCs and no transitive needs. but peering has limits for scale and requires route table updates. PrivateLink gives you an endpoint network interface in your VPC and is more controlled from a security perspective — good for restricting egress. Transit Gateway is our recommendation for customers with many VPCs or hybrid on-prem routing because it handles transitive routing and simplifies topology, but it's an extra AWS resource and has costs.
02:36 Michael: for us, transitive routing is important. we want to reach the Redwood infra from multiple accounts without opening a lot of peering. Transit GW sounds promising, but what about cross-region? we replicate us-east and eu-west.
02:49 Marcus: Transit Gateway supports inter-region peering but that adds latency and cost. an alternative is running regional Private deployments in each region and using internal replication or model sync. Another option is to front traffic through the nearest region and failover. Important: if you need data to never leave eu-west for EU customers, we can pin instances to region.
03:10 Priya: so you can pin model serving to a region and ensure data residency?
03:14 Marcus: yes, our Private deployment can be deployed into your VPCs in the specified region; we support region pinning to meet residency SLOs. There are network implications for model updates across regions but that's manageable.
03:28 Dana: How do we authenticate the control plane? we want a private control plane and not expose APIs to the public internet.
03:34 Sofia: for Private we offer a private control plane option — control traffic can traverse PrivateLink or we can deploy a control plane endpoint in your network via VPC endpoints. There is also an on-prem bundle if you want fully air-gapped.
03:48 Michael: KMS integration — we use a customer-managed KMS key. Can Redwood use our CMK/HSM for keys at rest?
03:55 Marcus: yes, we can integrate with a customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. for Private we typically support using your KMS keys for the storage volumes and secret store. HSM integrations are possible but normally a custom engineering effort — we'll flag that as a follow-up.
04:16 Dana: what about egress IPs? we need allowlisting so our firewall rules accept traffic from your service.
04:22 Marcus: we can provide a small set of static egress IPs when running in our managed-hosted mode, but in Private within your VPC the egress will be within your VPC NAT or IGW depending on routing. if you want outbound to be restricted we recommend using PrivateLink and restricting route tables so that traffic never goes to the public internet.
04:45 Priya: So for Private deployment inside our VPC, outbound egress is essentially under our control?
04:50 Marcus: Exactly. Everything is inside your networking fabric. Redwood processes run on instances in the VPC you provide or a dedicated account we attach to; network egress follows your routing.
05:02 Michael: Audit logs and access logs — we need request-level logs for compliance. Does Redwood provide audit trails for model access and admin actions?
05:10 Sofia: Yes, we emit audit logs and can forward to your central logging — CloudWatch, S3, or a SIEM. For Private we keep logs in your account/space so you control retention. we also have field-level logging options if you need to mask PHI.
05:25 Dana: what's the typical timeline to get a Private deployment up and running? assuming network is provisioned.
05:30 Marcus: generally 2-4 weeks for a standard Private deployment if network & IAM are ready. If you want on-prem or HSM integration, add 2-6 more weeks. We'll need network access, IAM roles, and a certificate exchange for mutual TLS if you're using PrivateLink.
05:46 Priya: what about patching and upgrades? we need clarity on who owns runtime updates for security patches.
05:52 Marcus: for Private we can offer two models: you manage the infra and we provide the software artifacts and instructions (self-managed), or Redwood operates the stack in your VPC with a managed operations agreement — we do patching and orchestration and provide runbooks. That's part of the Dedicated/Managed add-on.
06:09 Dana: cost — do we pay for raw infra only or a Redwood licensing fee on top?
06:15 Sofia: There is a platform fee for Private which includes software and support, plus the infra costs you run. For Dedicated it's a reserved capacity contract. We can send a detailed pricing sheet; I'll follow up.
06:25 Michael: network nitty gritty: do you support SAML/SSO for admin, and can we integrate with our IdP?
06:31 Sofia: yes, SSO via SAML/SCIM and RBAC for role-based permissions. For Private, SAML endpoints can be internal-only if your IdP is in the private network.
06:41 Michael: any known gotchas with CIDR/overlap?
06:44 Marcus: common gotchas: overlapping CIDRs prevent peering; in that case PrivateLink or a NAT-based pattern can help. Also ensure route table entries don't re-route traffic unexpectedly, and update security groups for intra-VPC traffic. if you use EKS with pod cidr overlap, we usually recommend a non-overlapping range for worker nodes.
07:05 Dana: We have an EKS cluster in prod with pod ranges already set. We'll share the VPC & pod cidrs.
07:12 Sofia: perfect. we'll provide a network checklist.
07:18 Marcus: another architectural detail: KV cache / session state — we use a distributed cache and for Private we can either colocate cache nodes inside your VPC or use your managed cache like Elasticache. that influences egress and data residency.
07:34 Michael: any changes needed to our firewall inspection appliances? we have an inline proxy and threat inspection that can break long-lived gRPC streams sometimes.
07:43 Marcus: good point. Redwood supports both gRPC streaming and HTTP streaming. if you have L7 proxies that terminate connections, you may need to allow long-lived connections or use a keepalive config. for problematic proxies, PrivateLink is often more resilient than NAT/IGW because endpoints look like normal ENIs.
08:05 Priya: latency — anything we should expect if we put the service in us-east versus eu-west for EU customers?
08:11 Marcus: regional latency is mostly network; serving in eu-west for EU customers is best for residency and latency. cross-region replication of model artifacts is asynchronous; if you serve across region boundaries you'll see additional tail latency for cold starts if KV caches need warm-up.
08:30 Dana: Are there examples of customers in healthcare doing Private deployments?
08:34 Sofia: yes, we have a couple of healthcare customers on Private. we can share anonymized architecture examples and references under NDA.
08:41 Michael: encryption in transit — mutual TLS?
08:44 Marcus: yes, we use mTLS for service-to-service communication and support mutual TLS for ingress if you want certificate-based auth. we can also integrate with your internal PKI.
08:56 Dana: logging again — how long do you retain request logs by default?
09:00 Sofia: default retention is 30 days in hosted; for Private, retention is controlled by you. we can configure S3 lifecycle to meet your retention policy.
09:10 Priya: any constraints on model size or GPU types in Private? can we bring our own model artifacts?
09:16 Marcus: we support a wide range of model sizes; for very large models you may want dedicated GPUs and we recommend quantization/throughput tuning. and yes you can bring your own model artifacts — we support a model onboarding process and version pinning. for very large models, disk IO and network bandwidth for model loads matter.
09:35 Dana: OK, let's talk about specific connectivity choices. our preference is Transit Gateway because we have multiple accounts. ops prefers not to maintain many peering connections.
09:45 Marcus: Transit Gateway + TGW attachments in each account is a common pattern. If you want PrivateLink, you'd set up an endpoint service in Redwood's account and create interface endpoints in your VPCs — that avoids TGW but requires an endpoint per VPC. For many VPCs, TGW is easier to manage.
10:03 Michael: For PrivateLink will the traffic be private to AWS? we worry if any control plane metadata flows to public endpoints.
10:09 Marcus: PrivateLink keeps data within AWS' private network. control plane communications are configurable; we can set up a private control plane so API calls don't traverse the public internet. we'll need to configure endpoint services and permissions.
10:22 Sofia: question for timeline — are you targeting a pilot before year-end?
10:25 Priya: yes, we'd like a pilot in Q4, ideally before Thanksgiving.
10:30 Sofia: that is doable if we get network details and IAM in the next week.
10:34 Dana: we'll aim to gather the CIDR ranges and VPN info by Friday.
10:38 Marcus: we'll produce a sample CloudFormation and Terraform module for the endpoint and a recommended security group template.
10:44 Sofia: we'll also share a checklist and pricing.
10:47 Dana: one more thing — do you support private endpoints for logs and metrics to feed into our SIEM buckets?
10:54 Marcus: yes, we can forward metrics/logs to your CloudWatch or push to S3 or an HTTP endpoint inside the VPC. for SIEM integration we typically ship via Kinesis or Firehose into your S3 bucket.
11:08 Michael: what are the credentials or roles we need to create?
11:11 Marcus: we'll request an IAM role for Redwood with a limited set of permissions (assume role) or we can operate in a dedicated account and cross-account role. the network checklist will specify the exact policies.
11:24 Dana: any enforcement or runtime auditing for model changes? we need to track who rolled out a new model and be able to rollback.
11:31 Sofia: yes, in the Console we have model versioning, rollout history, and can audit deployments. those artifacts can be forwarded to your logging.
11:39 Priya: licensing question — is there a minimum commit for Private?
11:43 Sofia: usually there is a base platform fee plus infra; for enterprise we can negotiate. i'll include that in the pricing email.
11:50 Dana: Security review — we'll need SOC2 docs and pen test reports.
11:54 Sofia: Absolutely. i'll send SOC2 and our security pack. we can do a security review session with your security team next week.
12:02 Michael: If we run a pilot, can we run some performance benchmarks — token latency and throughput?
12:07 Marcus: yes, we can run a benchmark in your VPC or replicate your workload with synthetic traces. we'll need sample prompt distribution and concurrency targets.
12:17 Dana: OK that would be helpful. we'll put together a juice of prompts and QPS numbers.
12:23 Sofia: Great. recap and next steps — here's what we'll do after this call: send pricing and SOC2, Marcus will create network diagrams and a TF/CF template, Aurora will send CIDRs and VPN info, and we'll schedule the SE deep dive next week.
12:40 Priya: sounds good.
12:42 Sofia: thanks everyone.
